key_insight: Neptuna introduces the first large-scale benchmark for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows and shows that model performance depends strongly on the dataset, metric, and loss design rather than any single architecture dominating.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives engineers a realistic way to compare surrogate models for complex multiphase phenomena like bubble collapse and droplet breakup, helping guide model choice for predictive design and simulation acceleration.
method: Built a 2.4 TB benchmark with high-fidelity 2D/3D shock-induced bubble collapse and droplet breakup data.
Compared convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models.
Tested MSE plus composite losses (Sobolev, interface-aware, structure-aware) with SoftAdapt and GradNorm weighting.
evidence_signal: Evaluation spans pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics, and the abstract reports that composite losses improve interface preservation and spectral fidelity while SoftAdapt gives the most consistent gains with minimal overhead.
watch_item: Because no single model or loss wins universally, deployment should be dataset-specific and carefully validated on interface and spectral behavior, not just MSE.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
